t: 3226. Number of Bit Changes to Make Two Integers Equal
o: We may only clear 1-bits of n. So n can become k iff every set bit of k is also set in n (k's bits are a subset of n's bits); otherwise -1. If possible, the number of changes is the count of bits set in n but not k, i.e. popcount(n XOR k) (which equals popcount(n) − popcount(k) under the subset condition). Examples: 13→4 clears two bits; 14→13 is impossible since 13 has bit 0 set but 14 doesn't.
k: No setting of bits is allowed, only clearing.

a.i: Two bitwise checks settle it: reject if k has a bit outside n, otherwise count differing bits. Built-in popcounts make this a few lines.
a.t: O(1) — a handful of word-level bitwise operations

w: Watch operator precedence: in C++/Java/JS, `~n` combined with `&` needs parentheses awareness (`k & ~n` parses correctly, but adding comparisons requires parens). Pitfall: answering popcount(n) − popcount(k) without the feasibility check. Follow-up: what if you could also set bits (then answer is popcount(n^k) unconditionally), or minimize changes with a limited budget?
